title: Book of Songs - Part 3
lines: One of the most beautiful aspects of the Book of Songs is how it captures the voices of ordinary people — farmers, soldiers, lovers, wives — across three thousand years of Chinese civilization.

The poems of the Shijing were collected by officials who traveled through the states, recording the songs of the common people. Confucius himself edited the collection from over three thousand poems down to three hundred and five.
Each poem in this section reveals a layer of ancient Chinese life: the rituals of the court, the ceremonies of the temples, the songs of the harvest, the laments of the separated lover.
To read the Book of Songs is to hear the heartbeat of ancient China — the joy, the sorrow, the longing, the reverence — all preserved in verses that have echoed through three millennia.
